market_name: Will 8 Fed rate cuts happen in 2026?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check 2y and 10y Treasury yields and fed funds futures for confirming downward move; verify no headline (jobs data, Fed speaker) already explains it.
time_plan.1h: Compare TLT move vs. rate-futures implied cuts; confirm the prediction-market shift is not stale/thin liquidity.
time_plan.2h: Reassess whether the dovish repricing is broadening across the curve or fading.
time_plan.6h: Check for scheduled economic releases or Fed communications that could validate the easing signal.
time_plan.12h: Evaluate whether TLT held the move; mark whether the prediction-market probability was a leading indicator or noise.

predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability of 8 rate cuts (200bps of easing) in 2026 signals expectations of aggressive Fed easing, typically tied to recession/labor-market deterioration or a dovish policy pivot. That drives front-end and long-end yields lower, pushing long-duration Treasury prices (TLT) up. The magnitude in a 12h window is modest because this market is about the full-year 2026 path, not an imminent catalyst.

predictions.tradable_instrument_name: Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check DXY and EUR/USD, JPY for confirming dollar weakness; verify no competing global driver.
time_plan.1h: Confirm dollar move aligns with lower US yields rather than global risk-off (which can strengthen USD).
time_plan.2h: Reassess whether risk-off vs. pure rate-differential dynamics dominate.
time_plan.6h: Check for overseas central-bank news that could offset the dollar signal.
time_plan.12h: Mark whether UUP direction matched thesis and whether magnitude stayed within interval.

predictions.reasoning: Pricing in 8 cuts implies a materially lower expected policy rate path, compressing US rate differentials and typically weakening the dollar. UUP would fall. Exposure is weaker/noisier than the direct rates channel because FX also depends on relative moves abroad and risk sentiment, so lower confidence.

evidence_used: Market question implies 8 cuts = 200bps of easing in 2026, an extreme dovish scenario
Aggressive-easing expectations historically co-move with falling yields, rising bond prices, and a weaker dollar
Topic tags (military_conflict) appear mislabeled; content is clearly a Fed monetary-policy market
uncertainty_notes: The 12h window is short relative to a full-year 2026 policy question, so any shift is a weak, diffuse signal
700bps tradable threshold is far above realistic 12h moves in these liquid proxies — neither prediction is 'tradable' under that bar
If the probability rises due to expected recession, risk-off could paradoxically strengthen USD, undermining the FX leg

llm_justification.summary: A sharp increase in the implied probability of 8 Fed rate cuts in 2026 signals aggressive-easing expectations, most cleanly mapping to lower Treasury yields (TLT up) and a modestly weaker dollar (UUP down). The rates channel is the more reliable link; the FX channel is noisier. Expected 12h magnitudes are small (tens of bps), well below the 700bps tradable threshold, so this is a directional research signal rather than an actionable trade.
key_assumptions: The prediction-market move reflects genuine shifts in easing expectations, not thin/illiquid noise
No overlapping public catalyst (jobs report, CPI, Fed speaker) already priced the move
Standard rate-differential and duration relationships hold over the window
failure_modes: Move already public: if a dovish data print or Fed comment preceded the market shift, proxies have already repriced
Reversal: extreme-cut markets are thin and mean-revert quickly, so early moves can fade
Weak proxy on FX: recession-driven easing bets can trigger safe-haven USD buying, flipping the UUP direction
Magnitude far below tradable threshold, so signal has no standalone execution value
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
